title: Extract bd-export-csv + dolt-remote-check into ~/Documents/degel/beads-utils with history
description:
Both utilities are beads/dolt-adjacent tools. Grouping them in their own repo (alongside blogscraper, degel-python-utils, fortune under ~/Documents/degel/) clarifies ownership and lets them grow without bloating ~/bin.

## Scope
- Use git filter-repo to extract the 3 commits that touched these files (1c43721, ce6469e, c2bd190) into a fresh history.
- Place files at the root of the new repo (not a subdirectory).
- Remove files from ~/bin with a normal 'git rm' commit (do NOT rewrite ~/bin's history).
- No new GitHub remote yet — leave for the user to 'gh repo create' later.
- No 'bd init' in the new repo yet — separate decision.

## Commits to carry
- 1c43721 Add dolt-remote-check
- ce6469e Add bd-export-csv
- c2bd190 bd-export-csv: --all + --sortby
close_reason: Extracted 3 commits into ~/Documents/degel/beads-utils (new SHAs, original authors/dates preserved). Old paths in ~/bin replaced with tiny forwarding stubs (shebang + 'moved to https://github.com/deg/beads-utils' message, exit 1) so published old-URL links keep resolving on GitHub.

title: bd-export-csv v2: switch to --all, add --sortby/--reverse
description:
Correction + enhancement to v1 (bin-cvg):

1. Export flags: misread user's 'ok' on bin-cvg — should have kept --all. Switch to 'bd export --all --no-memories' so infra/templates/gates are included.
2. Sorting: add --sortby=FIELD with choices id, title, type, status, priority, assignee, owner, created_at, updated_at, closed_at. Add --reverse for descending. Default: bd export's native order (no sort).

Sort implementation: after rows are built, str-coerce and stable-sort. str() handles mixed int (priority) vs string (all others) cleanly. Empty strings sort first ascending, last descending — intuitive for fields like closed_at.
notes: Design: --sortby takes comma-separated keys; '-' prefix = descending (e.g. 'priority,-created_at'). No separate --reverse flag — per-key direction subsumes it. Implementation: stable sort applied in reverse-key order. str() coercion handles mixed int (priority) vs string (dates, etc.) uniformly.
close_reason: --all added, --sortby KEYS (comma-separated, '-' prefix = desc) implemented. Verified priority-asc-then-created-desc grouping, leading-dash=form, error path, and help text. No separate --reverse flag.

title: bd-export-csv: export beads project state to CSV for review
description:
A personal tool at ~/bin/bd-export-csv that dumps every issue in a beads project to a CSV suitable for a project-review team to read in Google Sheets/Numbers/Excel.

Why: review teams want a single, filterable, printable view of project state. 'bd list' is too narrow; 'bd export' JSONL is not human-readable. A CSV with all interesting fields bridges the gap.

This is v1. Google Sheets auto-upload will come later as a separate issue; for now CSV is the deliverable.

## Scope
- Reads 'bd export --all --no-memories' JSONL from the target project.
- Writes a single CSV with one row per issue, all long-text fields included verbatim (newlines preserved via CSV quoting).
- Covers open + closed + deferred. No date cutoff.

## Invocation
- bd-export-csv [PROJECT_PATH] [-o OUTPUT]
- No arg -> uses current directory.
- Default output: <prefix>-issues-YYYY-MM-DD.csv in cwd.

## Columns
id, title, type, status, priority, assignee, owner, created_at, updated_at, closed_at, close_reason, labels, dependencies, spec_id, defer_until, external_ref, description, notes, design, acceptance_criteria, dependency_count, dependent_count, comment_count

- labels: pipe-joined ('phase-2|urgent')
- dependencies: pipe-joined '<type>:<depends_on_id>' pairs
- long text: verbatim, real newlines, csv.QUOTE_MINIMAL handles quoting
notes:
## Design decisions (pre-implementation)

- Python stdlib only (csv, subprocess, json, argparse, pathlib, datetime). No external deps, no venv. Shebang #!/usr/bin/env python3.
- Invokes 'bd export --no-memories' (default scope — excludes infra/templates/gates; --all would have included those and we don't want them for review).
- Output defaults to caller's cwd (not the project dir), so running from Desktop puts the CSV on Desktop.
- 'type' column maps from JSONL 'issue_type'.
- labels: pipe-joined sorted.
- dependencies: pipe-joined '<type>:<depends_on_id>' pairs. Example: 'blocks:mbz-d3j.1|parent-child:mbz-d3j'.
- Long-text fields (description/notes/design/acceptance_criteria): verbatim, real newlines, csv.QUOTE_MINIMAL. Google Sheets, Numbers, and Excel all import embedded-newline CSV correctly.
- Prefix for default filename derived from first issue's id; falls back to project directory name on empty project.
close_reason: v1 shipped. Script at ~/bin/bd-export-csv; smoke-tested against marketbuzzr (215 issues, 23 columns, embedded newlines and pipe-joined labels/deps verified). Google Sheets upload deferred to future issue.
